mutant.description: NOT a planted byte mutation, and the reason is recorded rather than glossed: every limb of this act's claim lives on the live S3/host plane or in an append-only shared file, so planting would have meant mutating served state or creating a transient false OPEN that a peer's `deploy_ledger.py check --red` sweep could escalate on. The DEPLOY genre exists for exactly this case (3.0.0_SA_CVO verdict 29306: 'a mutant has no meaning for a redeploy'), but it is NOT claimed, because the governing order carries <risk>WORLD</risk> and NO <proof_genre>DEPLOY</proof_genre> line at HEAD, and DEPLOY is never self-declared. The control used instead is STATE-BASED and arose naturally rather than being manufactured: r10.AC1 was run at three distinct states of the same act. AC1's load-bearing limbs are 'sentinel at HEAD=no' and 'listed OPEN/HELD=0', which together ARE the NEVER-2 closure claim, so those are the limbs exercised rather than an incidental one.
mutant.expected_not_landed: with the ledger open: sentinel at HEAD=yes; listed OPEN/HELD=1; RESULT: FAIL; exit=1
mutant.expected_landed: with the ledger closed and the deletion committed: sentinel at HEAD=no; listed OPEN/HELD=0; RESULT: PASS; exit=0
mutant.expected: AC1 reads FAIL while the entry is open and PASS once it is closed AND committed, with the two limbs flipping independently and in that order.
mutant.observed: FIRED, and it discriminated TWICE on different limbs. (1) Ledger OPEN, pre-close: 'sentinel at HEAD=yes; listed OPEN/HELD=1 -- RESULT: FAIL', exit=1 -- both limbs wrong. (2) Ledger CLOSED in the working tree but the deletion NOT yet committed: 'sentinel at HEAD=yes; listed OPEN/HELD=0 -- RESULT: FAIL', exit=1 -- the OPEN/HELD limb flipped while the HEAD limb did not, which is the sharpest available proof that AC1 grades COMMITTED state and not in-memory state. (3) After the close commit 87bf2c8723: 'sentinel at HEAD=no; listed OPEN/HELD=0 -- RESULT: PASS', exit=0. No live, shared or served state was mutated to produce any of the three readings.
